An Analytic Quantity Declared to a Tensor Stencil

Source: R/tensor.R
fd_known.Rd

Declares a function that returns analytic partial derivatives of the function differentiated by fd_tensor(), together with the multi-indices of the derivatives that it returns. fd_tensor() differences these values instead of the function itself wherever that leaves a lower order to the stencil.

Usage

fd_known(fun, order = NULL, indices = NULL)

Arguments

fun

A function of one argument, the named list of coordinates.

order

A single non-negative whole number, the total order of every derivative that fun returns, or NULL.

indices

An integer matrix of counts with one row per returned derivative and one column per coordinate, or NULL. Exactly one of order and indices is given.

Value

An object of class fd_known, with the properties fun, order and indices.

Details

A multi-index is a vector of counts, one per coordinate of x: the row c(2, 0, 1) over the coordinates (a, b, c) is \(\partial^3 f / \partial a^2 \partial c\). The rows of indices are the multi-indices of the values that fun returns, in the order in which it returns them. With order = k the rows are every multi-index of total order \(k\), in the order of tuple_indices(p, k) over the \(p\) coordinates; fd_tensor() expands the shortcut from the length of its x.

fun is called with a named list of the same shape as x and returns either a list of numeric vectors, one per row of indices, or a numeric matrix with one column per row, or a single vector when there is one row. Each vector has length 1 or \(n\). The names of the returned list are not read.

See also

fd_tensor(), which reads these declarations.

Examples

f <- function(x) x$a^3 * exp(x$b)
# the gradient is declared by its order
g <- fd_known(function(x) list(3 * x$a^2 * exp(x$b), x$a^3 * exp(x$b)),
              order = 1)
# the same quantity is declared by its multi-indices
g2 <- fd_known(function(x) cbind(3 * x$a^2 * exp(x$b), x$a^3 * exp(x$b)),
               indices = rbind(c(1, 0), c(0, 1)))
g2@indices
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    0
#> [2,]    0    1
